name: linear__prepare_attachment_upload
description:
Prepare a direct Linear file upload for an existing issue.
Uploaded files appear in the issue's Resources; they are not native Linear Documents. To embed a file in Markdown without adding it to an issue's Resources, use prepare_file_upload instead. For written findings or proposals, prefer updating the issue description or using save_document with issue to create an editable Linear Document, unless the user requests a file. The upload workflow creates the Resources link; do not also add the upload URL to save_issue's links field. To revise a file, upload a replacement. To remove its Resources link, use delete_attachment with the attachment ID returned by get_issue. These tools do not edit uploaded file contents, permanently delete stored files, or inspect or change per-file permissions. Explain these limits when relevant.

Workflow:
1. Call this tool with issue, filename, contentType, and size.
2. Upload raw bytes with PUT to uploadRequest.url outside MCP.
3. All headers in uploadRequest.headers are part of the signed request, so send them verbatim.
4. After PUT succeeds, call create_attachment_from_upload with assetUrl to link it to the issue.

Do not base64-encode or transform the file. Use curl --data-binary @path or fetch(url, { method: 'PUT', body: blob }).
Omitting or modifying any signed header, including casing, will return HTTP 403.
The signed URL must be used within 60 seconds or it will expire.

Upload sequencing:
Prepare, PUT, and finalize one file before calling this tool for another file.
Do not batch multiple prepare_attachment_upload calls before starting the PUTs because earlier signed URLs can expire while later files are prepared.

Example:
curl -X PUT --data-binary @file.png \
  -H "content-type: image/png" \
  -H "x-goog-content-length-range: N,N" \
  -H "cache-control: public, max-age=31536000" \
  -H 'Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="file.png"' \
  "<uploadRequest.url>"

issue.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues

filename.description: Filename for the upload, e.g. screenshot.png

contentType.description: MIME type, e.g. image/png or application/pdf

size.description: Exact file size in bytes. Must be smaller than 2 GB.

title.description: Suggested attachment title for the finalize step

subtitle.description: Suggested attachment subtitle for the finalize step

name: linear__create_attachment
description:
Deprecated fallback for tiny files only. Accepts base64 file content, verifies SHA-256 checksum, and uploads it through the MCP worker.
Prefer `prepare_attachment_upload` plus direct PUT plus `create_attachment_from_upload`.
Uploaded files appear in the issue's Resources; they are not native Linear Documents. To embed a file in Markdown without adding it to an issue's Resources, use prepare_file_upload instead. For written findings or proposals, prefer updating the issue description or using save_document with issue to create an editable Linear Document, unless the user requests a file. The upload workflow creates the Resources link; do not also add the upload URL to save_issue's links field. To revise a file, upload a replacement. To remove its Resources link, use delete_attachment with the attachment ID returned by get_issue. These tools do not edit uploaded file contents, permanently delete stored files, or inspect or change per-file permissions. Explain these limits when relevant.

CRITICAL: Do not print base64Content and then copy it into this tool call.
Opaque base64 copied through model-visible text is easy to corrupt.

Generate base64Content mechanically from the source bytes and pass it through a programmatic argument construction path whenever available. Before calling this tool, verify the values are consistent:

Unix-like shells:
file="/path/to/file"
base64Content=$(base64 < "$file" | tr -d '\n\r')
sha256=$(shasum -a 256 "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
decodedSha256=$(printf '%s' "$base64Content" | base64 -d | shasum -a 256 | awk '{print $1}')
size=$(wc -c < "$file" | tr -d ' ') # optional; stat can also get file byte size
decodedSize=$(printf '%s' "$base64Content" | base64 -d | wc -c | tr -d ' ')

PowerShell:
$file = 'C:\path\to\file'
$bytes = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes($file)
$base64Content = [Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes)
$sha256 = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -Path $file).Hash.ToLower()
$size = $bytes.Length # optional
$decoded = [Convert]::FromBase64String($base64Content)
$decodedStream = [IO.MemoryStream]::new($decoded)
$decodedSha256 = (Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -InputStream $decodedStream).Hash.ToLower()
$decodedSize = $decoded.Length

decodedSha256 must equal sha256. If you pass size, decodedSize must equal size.
Pass `sha256`. Passing `size` is optional, but recommended for clearer mismatch errors.

base64Content.description: Deprecated base64-encoded file content to upload

size.description: Optional expected decoded file size in bytes. Rejects the upload if it does not match.

sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 hex digest of the decoded file bytes.

name: linear__save_comment
description: Create or update a comment on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. If `id` is provided, updates the existing comment; otherwise creates a new one. To start a new thread, pass `body` and exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId` (`statusUpdateType` applies only to `statusUpdateId`; omit it for every other parent) — comments on issues/projects/initiatives become top-level discussion threads; comments on documents/milestones become description comments. A status update holds a single thread, so a comment on an update that already has one is added to it as a reply. To reply to an existing thread, pass `parentId` and `body`; the reply inherits the parent's thread type, so no entity reference is needed. Parent reference fields are ignored when `id` or `parentId` is provided (`statusUpdateType` is rejected instead). A new top-level comment starts a separate Linear thread and is not posted to a synced external thread. To post in a thread synced with Jira, Slack, or another service (for example, when asked to comment on the Jira thread), call `list_comments` on the issue, project, initiative, or status update that owns the thread. For project or initiative status updates, use `statusUpdateId`. Find the root comment (null `parentId`) whose body says the thread is synced with that service, and pass that root's `id` as `parentId`. When several threads match, such as an issue synced with more than one Jira issue, choose by the external link in the root's body. If no matching synced thread exists, do not post a top-level comment instead; report that no synced thread was found.

name: vercel__open_deployments
description: Use this when the user wants to see a Vercel deployment, check whether it is deployed, or follow its build: "show me deployments", "show me a live deployment", "show me UI deployments", "is it deployed yet?", or "watch this build". Fetches the latest matching deployment and renders an interactive live card with status, preview URL, commit, and expandable build logs. The user does not need to ask for a UI or card. Use the connection's project scope, or supply projectId (ID or name), repo, or a full commit sha. No prior deployment lookup is needed when that context is known. Optionally filter by branch, sha, or target environment. The card updates while the build runs; calling again updates the same project card. Use list_deployments for history or filtered lists, get_deployment for details by deployment ID or URL, list_deployment_events for build-failure investigation or log analysis, and get_runtime_logs for application runtime logs. Clients without app support receive a text summary.

teamId.description:
The ID or slug of the team that owns the resource.
Team IDs start with "team_".
If you do not know the team ID or slug, it can be found through these mechanism:
- Read the file .vercel/project.json if it exists and extract the orgId
- Use the `list_teams` tool
Optional: when omitted, the team is found from projectId.

projectId.description: The project ID or name. Read projectId from .vercel/project.json when the repository has one. Without it, pass repo for a preview instead of guessing, or use a project name the user gave. Required unless a preview call has repo or sha.

repo.description: Preview only. The git remote URL or owner/name (git remote get-url origin). Finds the linked project when projectId is unknown, even before the deployment exists.

target.description: Only consider deployments for this environment.

name: vercel__get_runtime_logs
description: Use this when reading application output (console.log, warnings, errors) that the functions and daemons of a project wrote at runtime, as individual log records, or when counting those records with group_by. Filter by deployment, environment, level, source, request ID, time range, or full-text query. The default window is the latest 50 minutes; for a recent window, pass since like "30m" and omit until, which is only needed for historical end times. How far back logs go depends on the runtime-log retention of the plan. For wide time ranges, scope to a deploymentId or use group_by. Do not use for build failures; use the deployment build logs instead. For clustered summaries of production errors, prefer get_runtime_errors.

projectId.description: The project ID (prj_...) or name to read runtime logs from.

teamId.description:
The ID or slug of the team that owns the resource.
Team IDs start with "team_".
If you do not know the team ID or slug, it can be found through these mechanism:
- Read the file .vercel/project.json if it exists and extract the orgId
- Use the `list_teams` tool

deploymentId.description: Only return logs from this deployment ID (dpl_...) or deployment URL.

level.description: Only return these log levels, for example ["error", "fatal"].

source.description: Filter by raw log source(s): function or daemon.

since.description: Start of the window as an ISO date or relative lookback from now (e.g., "15m", "30m"). Defaults to the 50 minutes before the earlier of until and now. Retention depends on your plan: Hobby keeps 1 hour, so longer lookbacks such as "6h" only work on plans that retain them.

until.description: Optional end of the window as an ISO date, relative lookback, or "now". Omit this when the end should be the current time.

limit.description: Maximum number of log entries to return. Defaults to 50, max 100.

query.description: Full-text search term that matching log records must contain, for example "ECONNRESET".

group_by.description: Return counts grouped by this attribute instead of individual log lines. Use for "how many errors", "source breakdown", "top paths". Fast even over wide time ranges.

name: vercel__get_runtime_errors
description: Use this when investigating production errors or finding the most frequent runtime failures in a project. Returns pre-aggregated error clusters with error names, occurrence counts, affected routes, sample messages, and first/last seen times. Use get_runtime_logs for individual log entries; use deployment build logs for build failures. For recent windows, pass since like "24h" or "7d" and omit until; until is only needed for historical end times. Max 7-day range.

projectId.description: The project ID to get runtime errors for.

name: vercel__get_project_trace
description: Get the resolved OpenTelemetry trace for a project by trace ID or Vercel request ID. Pass traceId (32-character hex, as in a dashboard URL ending in /logs/traces/<traceId>) or requestId (from runtime logs or the x-vercel-id header). Traces are only kept for the team plan's trace retention: 1 hour on Hobby, 1 day on Pro, 3 days on Enterprise. Internal Vercel runtime spans are removed and their children reparented; span durations are in milliseconds. Error spans include the type and stack trace of their first exception event. Returns at most 200 spans, keeping the root and error spans first; meta.omittedSpanCount reports how many were left out, and meta.partial is true when the trace exceeded the API's 10,000-span limit.

requestId.description: The Vercel request ID associated with the trace. Provide traceId or requestId.

name: vercel__get_access_to_vercel_url
description: Create or reuse a shareable link for a protected Vercel deployment that the user's Vercel account can access. Returns the deployment URL with a '_vercel_share' parameter. If no valid share link exists, one is created on the deployment, and anyone with the URL can view the deployment until it expires. New links expire in 23 hours; existing valid links keep their expiration and may not expire. Opening the URL redirects and sets an auth cookie; for clients without cookie support, web_fetch_vercel_url fetches the content directly.

teamId.description: The team ID or slug that owns the deployment. Provide this for team deployments so the lookup uses the correct scope. Use list_teams if unknown.

url.description: The full URL of the Vercel deployment (e.g. "https://myapp.vercel.app").

name: vercel__web_fetch_vercel_url
description: Fetch a Vercel deployment URL that the user's Vercel account can access, including deployments protected by Vercel Authentication, and return the response. To do so, it creates or reuses a temporary share link on the deployment (new links expire in 23 hours). Follows same-origin redirects only; a redirect to another origin is returned without being followed.

url.description: The full URL of the Vercel deployment including the path (e.g. "https://myapp.vercel.app/my-page").

name: vercel__authorize_team_sso
description:
Create a single-use Vercel consent link, valid for 10 minutes, to authorize this connection's existing app permissions for a team. Works for teams with or without SSO; the browser completes SSO when the team requires it. Does not grant access by itself.
Use when the connection lacks the target team's grant or its team SSO session has expired. The user opens the link and approves; afterward the original request can be retried on this same connection. A granted team is shared across this user's connections to the same app.

teamId.description: The ID or slug of the team to authorize, usually the `teamId` from the failed request.

Each submission also includes the MCP server version, the OAuth client ID, and the user, team, and project IDs when available. Retrying after an uncertain outcome can create a duplicate. Do not include secrets or personally identifiable information.

message.description: The feedback the user wants to send to Vercel.

context.description: Optional relevant details, such as the affected tool and expected behavior. Include only information the user intends to share.

name: vercel__get_purchase_quote
description: Get a read-only domain registration quote for the selected team. Checks availability and pricing and returns payment-method, tax/fee, registration, and auto-renew disclosures, plus a signed quote token valid for five minutes. Requesting a quote does not authorize a purchase, enable auto-renew, register, reserve, or charge for a domain. Digital subscriptions, credits, and add-ons cannot be quoted or purchased through this tool.

product.description: The kind of purchase to quote: a domain registration, which buy_domain completes after the user approves the quote.

teamId.description:
The ID or slug of the team that owns the resource.

- Use the `list_teams` tool

years.description: Registration term in years. Defaults to the TLD minimum.

autoRenew.description: Whether to auto-renew at term end. Defaults to true. Not part of the signed quote token.

name: vercel__buy_domain
description: Executes a single-domain registration previously quoted by get_purchase_quote (product:domain); this tool rejects calls without a valid quote. The quote is presented to the user for explicit approval, then this tool is called with confirm:true, the quote's idempotencyKey, the expectedPrice and years from the quote, and the full registrant contact supplied by the user. The purchase is charged immediately and is non-refundable. Vercel stores no reusable registrant profile, so contact details are required each time. The quote returns disclosures the user must see before approving: the payment method (default card on file), that taxes/fees may apply on top of the price, the item terms (non-refundable), and, when auto-renew is on, the recurring-charge terms in disclosures.subscription (renews automatically each term at the then-current price until auto-renew is turned off), plus a full-terms link.

years.description: Registration term in years. Required on confirm — must match the term shown in the quote.

autoRenew.description: Whether to auto-renew at the end of the term. Defaults to true.

expectedPrice.description: Required on confirm: the purchasePrice (USD) from the quote. The server rejects the order if it no longer matches the live price.

contact.description: Registrant (WHOIS) contact. Not needed for the quote; REQUIRED on confirm. All fields must be provided.

phone.description: Registrant's phone number in international E.164 format, e.g. +14155550123.

address1.description: Street address line of the registrant's postal address.

city.description: City of the registrant's postal address.

state.description: State, province, or region of the registrant's postal address.

zip.description: Postal or ZIP code of the registrant's postal address.

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code, e.g. US

companyName.description: Organization name for the registrant when registering on behalf of a company. Left out of the registrant contact when omitted.

name: vercel__start_board_thread

teamId.description:
The ID or slug of the team that owns the resource.
Team IDs start with "team_".
If you do not know the team ID or slug, it can be found through these mechanism:

- Use the `list_teams` tool

channel.description: The channel path, such as `dev` or `www/production`.

text.description: Markdown text, as the authenticated user. Everyone who can read the channel sees it, including its synced Slack, GitHub, or Linear threads. Mention people as `@handle`.

boardName.description: The board's name, as `vercel board --name` takes it, matched whatever its case. Defaults to the team's board; get_board_identity names it.

labels.description: The thread's labels, such as `{ "state": "open" }`. Change them later with label_board_message.

idempotencyKey.description: A random key you choose for this post. Retrying with the same key returns the first post instead of posting twice.

name: vercel__reply_to_board_thread
description: Reply in a Vercel board thread as the authenticated user. `messageId` is any message in the thread. Pass `ifLatestMessageId`, the `newestId` from get_board_thread, so the reply posts only if nobody wrote since; on a `newer_message` error, read the thread again before replying.

teamId.description:
The ID or slug of the team that owns the resource.
Team IDs start with "team_".
If you do not know the team ID or slug, it can be found through these mechanism:
- Read the file .vercel/project.json if it exists and extract the orgId
- Use the `list_teams` tool

messageId.description: A message ID as the board returns it, such as `msg_<uuid>_3`. Any message in a thread names that thread.

text.description: Markdown text, as the authenticated user. Everyone who can read the channel sees it, including its synced Slack, GitHub, or Linear threads. Mention people as `@handle`.

boardName.description: The board's name, as `vercel board --name` takes it, matched whatever its case. Defaults to the team's board; get_board_identity names it.

ifLatestMessageId.description: The ID of the thread's newest message as you read it (`newestId`, or the root's ID when it has no replies). The reply is rejected if a newer one exists.

idempotencyKey.description: A random key you choose for this post. Retrying with the same key returns the first post instead of posting twice.

name: vercel__label_board_message

With `if`, it changes them only while each listed label still has that value (`null` for unset); otherwise it fails with `label_conflict` and changes nothing.

teamId.description:
The ID or slug of the team that owns the resource.
Team IDs start with "team_".
If you do not know the team ID or slug, it can be found through these mechanism:

messageId.description: A message ID as the board returns it, such as `msg_<uuid>_3`. Any message in a thread names that thread.

if.description: Each label as it must be now, or `null` for not set, such as `{ "owner": null }` to claim an unowned thread.

boardName.description: The board's name, as `vercel board --name` takes it, matched whatever its case. Defaults to the team's board; get_board_identity names it.

name: vercel__wait_for_board_changes
description: Wait up to 25 seconds for new activity in a Vercel board channel or thread: posts, edits, deletes, reactions, and label changes. Pass `after` to continue from a returned `cursor` or a thread's `cursor` (or, on a thread, a message you just posted), so nothing in between is missed; without it, it starts from now. Call it again with each returned `cursor` to keep watching, about 24 calls per 10 minutes.

teamId.description:
The ID or slug of the team that owns the resource.
Team IDs start with "team_".
If you do not know the team ID or slug, it can be found through these mechanism:
- Read the file .vercel/project.json if it exists and extract the orgId
- Use the `list_teams` tool

channel.description: The channel path, such as `dev` or `www/production`. One channel, not a subtree. Pass this or `messageId`.

messageId.description: Only this message's thread: any message ID in it. Pass this or `channel`.

after.description: A cursor from an earlier call or from get_board_thread. When waiting on a thread, also any message ID in it, such as the one you just posted. Omit to start from now.

by.description: Only messages by this author: a handle, `me`, or an actor ID.

text.description: Only messages containing this text, case-insensitive.

label.description: Only messages with these labels on them or their thread root, each `key` or `key=value`.

wait.description: Seconds to wait when nothing is new, up to 25. Defaults to 25.

name: vercel__list_ai_gateway_virtual_models
description: Use this when finding a team's Vercel AI Gateway virtual models, the reusable model configurations that requests call as vmc/<slug>. Returns each one's ID, slug, kind, display name, description, status, and the names of up to 20 target models with the total as modelCount, ordered by slug, with a nextCursor when more remain. Virtual models with status archived are left out unless includeArchived is true. Use get_ai_gateway_virtual_model for one model's full routing configuration. The public model catalog is separate and does not include virtual models. Fails with a permission error when the connection has no AI Gateway virtual model access or is limited to selected projects.

teamId.description: The ID (team_...) or slug of the team that owns the AI Gateway configuration. Use list_teams to discover an unknown team.

includeArchived.description: Also return virtual models whose status is archived.

limit.description: Maximum virtual models to return. Defaults to 25. Use a smaller value when a page is refused as too large.

cursor.description: The nextCursor from the previous call, to get the next page. Omit for the first page.

name: vercel__get_ai_gateway_virtual_model
description: Use this when reading the full configuration of one Vercel AI Gateway virtual model: its target model or models, provider order and restrictions, inference region, caching, service tier, timeouts, and data-retention settings. Pass the slug with or without the vmc/ prefix; use list_ai_gateway_virtual_models to discover it. Returns the stored configuration without the IDs of the people who changed it. In the free-form provider and selector options, a value that its key or its own text marks as a credential is replaced with [redacted]. Text is cut at 500 characters. A configuration above the size limit is returned without the values that do not fit, and marked truncated. This reads configuration only, not the model's spend or traffic.

teamId.description: The ID (team_...) or slug of the team that owns the AI Gateway configuration. Use list_teams to discover an unknown team.

slug.description: The virtual model slug, such as fast-chat or vmc/fast-chat.

name: vercel__list_ai_gateway_rules
description: Use this when checking how a team's Vercel AI Gateway routing rules change or block model requests. Returns each rule's ID, type (rewrite sends a matched model to another model; deny rejects it), match, action, enabled state, and description, oldest first, with a nextCursor when more remain. shadowedBy names the rule that takes precedence for the same model, so the listed rule never applies. Disabled rules are left out unless includeDisabled is true. Rules apply to the whole team.

teamId.description: The ID (team_...) or slug of the team that owns the AI Gateway configuration. Use list_teams to discover an unknown team.

includeDisabled.description: Also return rules that are turned off.

limit.description: Maximum rules to return. Defaults to 25. Use a smaller value when a page is refused as too large.

cursor.description: The nextCursor from the previous call, to get the next page. Omit for the first page.

name: vercel__list_ai_gateway_budgets
description: Use this when checking a team's Vercel AI Gateway spend limits and how much of each is used. Returns the budgets set for the team, its projects, members, and API keys: the limit and current spend in USD, the BYOK spend, the refresh period, and whether the budget is active. Budgets that a scope inherits from a default are not listed; defaultCoveredCounts gives their number per scope type. Pass scopeType to return one kind. Pass scopeId to return one project's, member's, or API key's budget, including an inherited one, which is marked source: default. Set defaults to true to return the per-scope default budgets instead. Budgets cap spend; they do not show which models the spend went to.

teamId.description: The ID (team_...) or slug of the team that owns the AI Gateway configuration. Use list_teams to discover an unknown team.

scopeId.description: Only the budget of this project ID (prj_...), user ID, or API key ID. The result is empty when that scope has no budget. Ignored when defaults is true.

defaults.description: Return the default budgets that apply to every project, member, or API key without its own budget, instead of individual budgets. Not paged.

limit.description: Maximum budgets to return. Defaults to 25. Use a smaller value when a page is refused as too large.

cursor.description: The nextCursor from the previous call, to get the next page. Omit for the first page.

name: vercel__list_ai_gateway_models
description: Use this when choosing a model on Vercel AI Gateway or checking what one costs. Searches the live public catalog and returns each match's ID, type, context window, output limit, model-specific pricing in USD, and capability tags, with the total number of matches and, when more remain, a nextOffset to pass as offset for the next page. Use get_ai_gateway_model for the providers that serve one model. This is reference data; it does not read the user's account, so a team's virtual models (vmc/...) are not listed.

query.description: Case-insensitive text to find in the model ID or name, such as "claude" or "gpt-5".

limit.description: Maximum models to return. Defaults to 25.

offset.description: Models to skip. Pass the nextOffset from the previous call to get the next page.

name: vercel__get_ai_gateway_model
description: Use this when comparing the providers that serve one Vercel AI Gateway model. Returns the model's description and, for each provider endpoint, its pricing in USD, context and output limits, supported parameters, zero-data-retention and no-training flags, uptime, latency, and throughput. Use a known creator/model ID directly; use list_ai_gateway_models only when you need to discover it. This is reference data; it does not read the user's account.

modelId.description: The model ID as creator/model, such as openai/gpt-5.

name: vercel__get_ai_gateway_leaderboard
description: Use this when asking which models, model labs, apps, or inference providers are most used on Vercel AI Gateway. models and labs return each name's percentage share of one metric on one day, highest first: requests on the most recent day unless metric, modality, or date say otherwise. apps and providers return two top-10 lists of names, one ranked by token volume and one by spend, told apart by ranked_by. When more rows remain, pass the returned nextOffset as offset. The data is open and anonymized (CC BY 4.0) and covers all of AI Gateway, not the user's account; use get_ai_gateway_usage for that. App names are supplied by third parties.

metric.description: What models and labs are ranked by. Defaults to requests. Ignored for apps and providers.

modality.description: Only count text, image, or video usage, for models and labs. Defaults to all. A metric the modality does not have, such as tokens for video, returns no rows. Ignored for apps and providers.

date.description: The day to return for models and labs, as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the most recent day. Ignored for apps and providers.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 25.

offset.description: Rows to skip. Pass the nextOffset from the previous call to get the next page.

name: vercel__get_ai_gateway_usage
description: Use this when measuring a team's Vercel AI Gateway spend, request volume, token usage, or latency. Returns totals for the chosen metrics, optionally grouped by one dimension such as model or provider, plus an hourly or daily series when granularity is set. Covers the last 7 days by default. A scoped connection fixes the team/project; otherwise, pass projectId to limit the team query to one project. Returns aggregates only, never prompts or responses; use get_ai_gateway_leaderboard for usage across all of AI Gateway.

teamId.description: The team ID (team_...) for team-wide usage. A team slug is supported only together with projectId. Use list_teams to discover an unknown team ID.

projectId.description:
Only usage from this project. Omit for the whole team only when the connection is not already scoped to a project.
The ID or slug of the project.
Project IDs start with "prj_".
If you do not know the project ID or slug, it can be found through these mechanism:
- Read the file .vercel/project.json if it exists and extract the projectId
- Use the `list_projects` tool

since.description: Start of the window as an ISO date or relative lookback from now (e.g. "24h", "7d"). Defaults to 7 days before until.

until.description: Optional end of the window as an ISO date, relative lookback, or "now". Omit this when the end should be the current time.

metrics.description: Metrics to return. Defaults to cost and count. cost is billed spend in USD, count is requests, the token metrics are sums, and the two _ms metrics are averages. Groups are ranked by the first metric.

groupBy.description: Break the totals down by this dimension.

granularity.description: Also return a time series with this bucket size. The window can span at most 100 buckets. For hour, specify a window of at most 100 hours (e.g. since: "24h"); use day for the default 7-day window. The window is widened to whole UTC buckets, and the returned start and end show the widened window.

limit.description: Maximum groups to return. Defaults to 10.

name: vercel__aggregate_events
description: Counts custom events on a project, within the requested date range. Results are either aggregated or broken down over time. Results can additionally be broken down by one dimension, and filtered by multiple dimensions.

projectId.description: The project identifier or the project name

items.errorMessage: `by` items should be equal to one of the allowed values "hour, day, week, month, year, country, deviceType, environment, requestPath, referrerHostname, osName, browserName, route, utmSource, utmMedium, utmCampaign, utmContent, utmTerm, eventName, flags, eventData", or a JSON dimension key such as "flags/<name>, eventData/<property>"

by.description:
Up to two dimensions used to break down results.

At most one time granularity is allowed: hour, day, week, month, year.

Other dimensions: country, deviceType, environment, requestPath, referrerHostname, osName, browserName, route, utmSource, utmMedium, utmCampaign, utmContent, utmTerm, eventName.

JSON dimensions: flags, eventData. Used bare, they break down results by key, for example flags returns one group per flag name. With a key, they break down results by that key's value, for example eventData/plan. Wrap keys containing characters other than letters, digits, and underscores in single quotes, for example flags/'my-flag'.

since.description:
Timestamp in milliseconds, or a valid Date string.

Selects data from (including) this date and time.
Will be adjusted according to the desired time granularity.

until.description:
Timestamp in milliseconds, or a valid Date string.

Selects data until (including) this date.
Will be adjusted according to the desired time granularity.

limit.description: Number of distinct results, default to 10. Other results are grouped into "Others" group.

filter.description:
OData-compliant filter. Encode the value when sending it in a URL.

Allows filtering on one or multiple dimensions. By default, filters for production environment only.

Supported dimensions: country, deviceType, environment, requestPath, referrerHostname, osName, browserName, route, utmSource, utmMedium, utmCampaign, utmContent, utmTerm, eventName.

JSON dimensions filtered by key: flags/<name>, eventData/<property>, for example eventData/plan eq 'pro'. Wrap keys containing characters other than letters, digits, and underscores in single quotes, for example flags/'my-flag' eq 'true'.

Supported operations include eq, ne, in, and logical operators and, or, not with parentheses. Functions such as startswith are supported by the OData parser.

teamId.description: Team ID to use for this operation.

slug.description: Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.

name: vercel__create_ai_gateway_rule
description: Use this when adding a Vercel AI Gateway routing rule that sends requests for one model to another model (type rewrite) or rejects them (type deny). The rule applies to every request of the whole team. Needs teamId or slug to name the team; the call fails without one. requestBody needs type and match.model. A rewrite rule also needs action.rewriteModel: a catalog model ID, or a virtual model as vmc/<slug> (from list_ai_gateway_virtual_models). That model must exist and be active. A deny rule can give action.reason. The rule is enabled unless enabled is false. Fails with a conflict when a rule of the same type already exists for the model; change that rule with update_ai_gateway_rule. The result is the rule as list_ai_gateway_rules returns it. Confirm with list_ai_gateway_rules, where shadowedBy names a rule that takes precedence.

reason.description: Why the model is denied. Used when `type` is `deny`.

name: vercel__create_ai_gateway_virtual_model
description: Use this when creating a Vercel AI Gateway virtual model, a reusable model configuration that every request of the team can call as vmc/<slug>. Needs teamId or slug to name the team; the call fails without one. Here slug is the team slug, not the virtual model slug. requestBody needs virtualModelSlug and modelSlug, the model that it resolves to. Optional fields set fallback models, provider order and restrictions, inference region, caching, service tier, timeouts, and data-retention limits. It serves requests when status is active, which is the default. Fails with a conflict when the slug is in use, also by a deleted virtual model; restore that one with update_ai_gateway_virtual_model. Fails with a permission error when the connection has no AI Gateway virtual model write access or is limited to selected projects. The result is the configuration as get_ai_gateway_virtual_model returns it, with the same redaction, inside the catalog size limits.

A move-in changes ownership within Vercel and requires a pending move approval for the receiving account. Neither method purchases a domain or transfers its registration from an external registrar. Domains acquired outside MCP can be added with method:add.

name: vercel__upsert_ai_gateway_budget
description: Use this when setting or changing a Vercel AI Gateway spend limit for a whole team, one project, or one team member. Needs teamId or slug to name the team; the call fails without one. Creates the budget for that scope or replaces the existing one, and makes an archived budget active again. requestBody needs scopeType and limitAmount in USD (minimum 1), with projectId for scope project (from list_projects) or userId for scope user (the uid from list_team_members). Each call sets the whole budget: an omitted refreshPeriod becomes monthly and an omitted includeByokInQuota becomes false. Omitted alertThresholds keep their value. A caller without permission to change team budgets can change only their own user budget, when the team allows it, and must give justification. The result is a row as list_ai_gateway_budgets returns it, but its currentSpend is always 0: read the spend with list_ai_gateway_budgets. This does not set API key budgets; use upsert_ai_gateway_budget_default for a default budget.

teamId.description: Team ID to use for this operation.

slug.description: Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.

projectId.description: Required when scopeType is \"project\".

includeByokInQuota.description: Whether BYOK usage counts toward this budget.

justification.description: Why the budget is being changed, up to 500 characters. Recorded in the activity log and audit log drains, and sent in the ai-gateway.budget.updated webhook.

name: vercel__upsert_ai_gateway_budget_default
description: Use this when setting a default Vercel AI Gateway spend limit for a team: the limit of every project, every team member, or every API key that has no budget of its own. Needs teamId or slug to name the team; the call fails without one. requestBody needs scopeType (project, user, or api-key) and limitAmount in USD (minimum 1). Creates the default for that scope or changes its limit. It does not reset the other settings: omitted refreshPeriod and alertThresholds keep their stored values, and a new default is monthly. Needs permission to change team budgets. Confirm the change with list_ai_gateway_budgets and defaults:true. To limit the team itself, one project, or one member, use upsert_ai_gateway_budget.

teamId.description: Team ID to use for this operation.

slug.description: Team slug to use for this operation. Use instead of teamId.

justification.description: Why the budget is being changed, up to 500 characters. Recorded in the activity log and audit log drains, and sent in the ai-gateway.budget.updated webhook.

name: vercel__upload_artifact
description: Upload a remote cache artifact, provided as base64 content, stored under the given hash. Optional inputs record the artifact's size, generation time, CI environment, and source revision.

xArtifactDuration.description: The time taken to generate the uploaded artifact in milliseconds.

xArtifactClientCi.description: The continuous integration or delivery environment where this artifact was generated.

xArtifactClientInteractive.description: 1 if the client is an interactive shell. Otherwise 0

xArtifactTag.description: The base64 encoded tag for this artifact. The value is sent back to clients when the artifact is downloaded as the header `x-artifact-tag`

xArtifactSha.description: The SHA of the source control revision that generated this artifact.

xArtifactDirtyHash.description: A hash representing uncommitted changes in the working directory when this artifact was generated.
